bug_semantics: MISP expansion module html_to_markdown accepted an attacker-controlled HTTP(S) URL from the module request JSON and fetched it with requests.get(url) in fetchHTML() with no scheme allowlist, no loopback/private/link-local blocklist, no DNS resolution before fetch, and no timeout. A caller who can submit a URL attribute for expansion can coerce the module worker to request internal network resources (CWE-918 SSRF) and receive the response converted to markdown. Independently, qrcode.fetch_url_image() retrieved remote images with requests.get(..., verify=False), disabling TLS certificate validation (CWE-295) and exposing the download to MITM tampering. CVE-2026-44363 is published on CVE.org (GitHub_M CNA, state PUBLISHED); GHSA-fhq3-2gf3-8f3j withdrawn_at is null.
flaw_origin: The SSRF sink was first written when Sami Mokaddem added html_to_markdown as a new expansion module on 2020-10-23: fetchHTML() was born as an unvalidated requests.get(url) and handler() passed request['url'] straight into it. That GET line was never rewritten; a 3.x style pass (1062a8543fd25e05f9da972d27a836ff172abf36) and a later raw_html input path (728e38ac27e003bfd2c3abe9ede5ce23dfbc386a) left fetchHTML unchanged until the 2026-04-29 security patch. The qrcode verify=False call is a second, later sink introduced on 2026-02-10 in 925e2e8089a0676b4bad2be4bafda9897346b906 when remote URL fetching was added to that module; it is additional advisory surface, not the first write of the html_to_markdown SSRF.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-44363 is a real published SSRF plus improper TLS validation in misp-modules expansion helpers, not a withdrawn/rejected advisory. The html_to_markdown attack path is request JSON url -> handler() -> fetchHTML() -> requests.get(url) with no allow/deny controls, which at v3.0.7 is still exactly that one-liner. git log -L/:S show that line was born in 2be1d7a0cde74703e15e2afd70c4205d9a4c3844 when the module file was added; the immediate parent tree lacks the file and any fetchHTML, so this is a first-write BIC rather than a move, refactor, revert, or squash. Later 3.x formatting and the raw_html feature did not rewrite the sink. The qrcode verify=False path is a distinct later introduction (925e2e8) bundled in the same GHSA; it does not displace the 2020 SSRF BIC. The advisory-linked SHA 01a522f is a Black reformat of the already-patched file; the matching remediation (scheme check, private-range block, DNS resolve-before-fetch, timeout, re-enable TLS verify), credited to the same reporter, is 52cda9caa003cafe87e14ae3721db5e16f6f111a, a non-merge commit first released in v3.0.8, so that SHA is both fix_sha and direct_fix_sha. AI is judged only from the BIC commit object: human CIRCL author/committer mokaddem in 2020, no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot markers. Later AI-looking style work on qrcode or the 2026 fix commit cannot attribute the introducer. Verdict is therefore NOT_AI.
